reports.title: Weibo Announces Third Quarter 2026 Unaudited Financial Results

desk.headline: Revenue down 7% to $410.2m and adjusted EPS down to $0.06 from $0.42, both missed; no guidance, management cautious on Q4

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted (non-GAAP) diluted; GAAP diluted EPS $0.10 vs $0.83

results: Revenue fell 7% to $410.2m (down 13% at constant exchange rates); advertising dropped 8% to $344.1m as e-commerce, gaming and cosmetics brands spent less.
Ad spending from Alibaba fell 33% to $30.5m against a high base last year; other advertisers were down 5%.
Costs rose 6% on higher ad-production spending, so the adjusted operating margin shrank to 17% from 30%.
Adjusted profit collapsed to $14.3m ($0.06 a share) from $110.7m; GAAP profit was $24.5m ($0.10) versus $221.1m, which had been lifted by investment gains.
Operations used $10.2m of cash in the quarter; Weibo still holds $2.31bn of cash and short-term investments.

guidance.summary: Weibo does not give numerical guidance. On the call management said it is staying cautious and expects soft advertiser demand and cost pressure to continue into the fourth quarter.

points: Management expects ad demand in most traditional sectors to stay weak, with little near-term visibility; car, handset, internet and food & beverage advertisers grew, e-commerce and cosmetics fell.
Q4 faces a tough comparison with last year's food-delivery ad surge, plus cautious Double 11 shopping-festival budgets and handset launch timing.
AI is used across content, ads and operations; about half of feed and performance-ad creative is now AI-generated, and a new automated ad-placement tool launched late in Q3.
Users dipped: daily users were 254m (down 1% y/y), blamed on weaker phone shipments and fewer big trending topics; more video creators were signed up.
Management said overall ad revenue growth is likely to stay under pressure into 2027.
call.source: Call coverage: The Motley Fool call transcript and Investing.com call report, 17 Nov 2026

watch: Whether ad revenue stabilises in Q4 against the high food-delivery base.
Margin recovery after costs rose while revenue fell.
User numbers and the payoff from AI ad tools.
